correctness.rationale: Degree-m Bernstein functions form a basis of restrictions to the simplex by homogenizing with (sum p_s)^(m−degree); homogeneous independence follows by scaling from the simplex interior. The Dirichlet reference has full support, so the Gram form is positive definite and the dual exists uniquely, including the one-point simplex. Summing Bernstein functions gives normalization at every k, including k=0. Multiplying the degree-k monomial by (sum p_s)^(m−k) gives the stated degree-elevation coefficients and thus hypergeometric conservativity. Under normalized independent gammas with positive shapes, the within-group proportions are independent of the group totals and have the restricted Dirichlet laws. Conditional moments of p^r are constants times merged-p^r', so the expected dual has degree at most m. The multinomial grouping identity tests it against the entire coarse degree-m basis and gives exactly the coarse dual with summed shapes. Testing at degree k then proves the merge law without a degree restriction on k. For the obstruction let z=p_c; the dual moments through degree three are 1,1/3,0,0 for either reference. Integrating the displayed monic quartics against z^j, j=0,1,2,3, using Beta(1,2) moments 2/[(j+1)(j+2)] and Beta(1,1) moments 1/(j+1) confirms their orthogonality. The degree-four moment L(z^4) is therefore 1/18 or 17/210. If a denotes that moment, the five probabilities are (a,−4a,6a,4/3−4a,a−1/3), giving both stated vectors and half-l1 distance 64/315. With at most two colors every merge is a bijection or collapses to one color; three full-support colors require m≥3, and k≤m already commutes, proving minimality under the stated full-support condition.
residual_risks: Finite checks are corroborative, not the general proof. The intrinsic choice α=β needs strictly positive counts; α must remain positive even when β is allowed to have zeros. The result concerns deterministic color merges, not stochastic relabeling.
